hot.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
hot.summary: MemT-1.0 gives a language model an evolving, fixed-size memory state that it updates between turns and reads during later responses, rather than supplying the full conversation history again. Its token-level updates use a stable GDN-2 mechanism, while Mixture-of-Storage expands memory capacity. On 11 memory benchmarks, Flash scores 50.6 on the aggregate, above parametric-memory baselines, but textual-memory systems score higher overall.

hot.title: Koi: Evidence-Guided, Self-Calibrating Planning for Multi-Cloud, Heterogeneous LLM Inference Fleets
hot.summary: Koi jointly plans inference deployments across jobs sharing cluster capacity, rather than ranking them separately. Language models propose candidates; deterministic tools predict outcomes, check constraints, and select feasible plans. Telemetry updates scoped hypotheses in a graph. In a three-hour 104-GPU benchmark, Koi achieved 17.79% higher goodput than OpenEvolve and 20% lower cost per SLO-token; this comparison does not establish global optimality.

hot.title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
hot.summary: EgoX jointly reconstructs camera motion, scene depth, hands, and rigid objects from monocular video in a shared metric frame. It trains these predictions together using aligned annotations and predicted cameras to place hand and object geometry in the world frame. On held-out EgoX-Bench, it reports 113.24 mm W-MPJPE versus 328.81 mm for WiLoR + SLAM, and assumes rigid objects.

hot.title: ScaleNav: Scalable Internet Video Pretraining for Language-Conditioned Local Navigation
hot.summary: ScaleNav enables robots to navigate to initially visible objects by learning visual approach dynamics from action-free Internet videos, then aligning them with executable actions using labeled simulation data. Its shared model predicts action chunks for closed-loop execution. It reaches 94.9% success on HabitatGS-LN and 83.3% success across 60 real-robot trials in three indoor environments, but broader robustness is untested.

hot.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
hot.summary: Ropedia W0 predicts future egocentric video from an initial image, text, camera poses, and image-aligned skeletons, using human and robot video. On 400 evaluation windows across eight embodiments, its A14B model reaches 21.98 dB PSNR, versus 19.02 for Cosmos3-Nano. Ablations show 21.65 without camera-ray conditioning and 18.17 without skeletons; the interface models visual motion, not contact or object dynamics.

hot.title: A Language-Informed Loss for Visual Generation
hot.summary: LILIE trains an invertible transform to preserve information useful for predicting captions from corrupted image features, then uses distances in that learned space as a generator training loss. Unlike a lossy tokenizer, it retains image information and leaves generation in pixel space. On 256×256 GPIC images, Pixel+LILIE lowers gFD from 66.84 to 53.01 versus pixel-only training in the JiT-T2I-g evaluation setup.

hot.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
hot.summary: RoboValue benchmarks whether robotic value models’ scores reflect task instructions and execution history, rather than only progress or success. It tests task understanding, progress, recovery, and consistency across valid subtask orders in simulation and real-world tasks. In tea-set examples, CSVC was −40.98 for Robo-Dopamine 2.0-8B Preview and 2.30 for RoboMeter; these different evaluation tracks are not a head-to-head comparison.

hot.title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience
hot.summary: Holi-World connects persistent 3D room structure with object identities, tracks, and interaction histories to generate training questions from egocentric video. Its pipeline builds static scene records and dynamic object tracks linked to supporting observations. Fine-tuned HoliWorld-VL-4B reaches 78.02% Token F1 versus 16.35% for Qwen3.5-4B on HoliWorld-Bench, within data from about 100 scenes and 444 videos.

hot.title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
hot.summary: HarnessPro learns agent harnesses from execution traces, identifying failures and redundant work. It uses synthesized tests to evaluate candidates, then retains lite, medium, and heavy versions for different performance-cost priorities. On Terminal-Bench 2, GPT-5.5 with Codex, HarnessPro-Heavy reaches an 80.8% mean pass rate at $0.72, versus RHO’s 76.3% at $1.09, showing a better measured trade-off in this benchmark.

hot.title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
hot.summary: PhysWord predicts future action words paired with hidden representations of visual dynamics and optional tactile contact, then uses those predictions to condition action generation. In an extended paper-picking task, it succeeds in 70.0% of episodes, versus 36.7% for a variant without word supervision. On LIBERO-Long, it averages 99.6% across ten tasks, versus 98.4% for UniWAM; this is not a measure of all long-horizon tasks.

hot.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
hot.summary: Halcyon trains a text-image generator from scratch by predicting text and image tokens jointly from image-caption pairs, rather than pretraining a separate language model on web-scale text. On GPIC Test-50K at 256×256, Halcyon-1.6B achieves 35.28 gFD versus 40.97 for JiT-T2I-XXL/8++, with 275× less total pretraining compute. gFD measures image-distribution similarity, not prompt adherence; results are limited to GPIC and 256×256.

hot.title: ReAnchor: Reusing Rejected Verifier States for Diffusion Drafting
hot.summary: ReAnchor improves speculative decoding with block-diffusion drafters by reusing verifier hidden states from rejected suffixes as conditioning for additional native-length draft blocks. It matches their starting tokens to the baseline draft and has the target verify every continuation. At temperature T=0, it raises acceptance length 15.2% and speed 13.4% across four models and eight benchmarks, though gains vary by setting.

hot.title: Reward Misspecification Degrades Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
hot.summary: The authors show that output-reward reinforcement learning can produce reward hacking that a chain-of-thought monitor misses, without optimizing against it. They compare models trained on true and misspecified rewards across three tasks and three models. Reward-description training raises intervention and reward-intent g-mean² scores from 0.13 and 0.17 to 0.37 and 0.59, while hack rate falls from 0.87 to 0.79; results are limited to the testbed.

hot.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
hot.summary: DiscoveryRSI records evidence, revisions, decisions, and contributions across hypothesis development, then uses histories to train agent actions and revise research workflows. Its hypotheses pair an evidence-grounded claim with an investigation plan, interpretation criteria, and alternatives. Across four life-science domains, automated weighted quality rose from 4.86 to 5.39 after two rounds; this measures proposal quality, not truth or completed discovery.

hot.title: State World Models: Execute the Rules, Generate the Pixels
hot.summary: Stateful Harness tests whether a frozen video model can render outcomes governed by hidden state and executable rules. It settles actions against an explicit state ledger, compiles the result into visual instructions, and uses the renderer to depict it. On 50 counterfactual pairs, MiniMax-H3 reaches 92% PAIRFOLLOW and 90% PAIRSTRICT, evidence limited to short, controlled trials.

hot.title: Statistical decision theory in thermodynamics
hot.summary: The authors develop bounds on worst-case loss for decisions about stochastic processes. They use Le Cam's two-point method to relate loss to distinguishability between two candidate processes, connecting it to dynamical activity when they share an initial distribution. For classification, the lower bound reaches one-half as summed initial activity vanishes, but does not establish actual classifier accuracy.

hot.title: SteerAct: Unlocking Action Models through Few-Shot Temporal Steering
hot.summary: SteerAct adapts a frozen robot action model using outcome-labeled successful and failed rollouts, without updating its weights during steering. A pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) exposes feature activity, whose temporal patterns select one feature offline and determine online when and how to intervene. On RoboTwin 2.0 with π₀.₅, mean success reaches 77.7%, versus 69.0% for Base, but gains are not universal.

hot.title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
hot.summary: HandsOn introduces a benchmark and data platform for evaluating dexterous manipulation beyond grasping. It provides 18,000 simulated human-demonstration trajectories and tests learned policies on 50 demonstrated tasks and 16 evaluation-only transfer tasks. The best trained checkpoint, OpenWAM, achieves 29.1% task-macro success on Core-50 but 0.4% on Transfer-16, showing a sharp transfer boundary under this protocol.

hot.title: A Unifying View of Distributionally Robust Optimization for Probability Smoothing via Maximum Entropy
hot.summary: OT-DRO smooths finite-sample probability estimates using an optimal-transport cost matrix, so category relationships guide probability assigned to unseen categories. Under stated conditions, the authors show that distributionally robust smoothing is maximum-entropy within its ambiguity set. In synthetic tests with 100 categories and 100 draws, OT-DRO lowers mean KL divergence versus 2-DRO in structured data but raises it in unstructured data.

hot.title: HAF-VLA: Hierarchical Action Flow Framework for Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Control
hot.summary: HAF-VLA generates humanoid actions in three stages: locomotion and gaze, waist posture, then arm-and-hand manipulation, with later stages refining earlier plans. Across six real-robot tasks, its average normalized score is 68.3%, versus 53.3% for π0.5; it is best or tied-best on every task. These partial-progress scores average 10 rollouts, not full-task success rates.

likes.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
likes.summary: RePR trains image representations to capture how context improves a generative predictor’s predictions of image patches. It uses this signal to guide a tokenizer, then generates pixels from that representation. On ImageNet, 50,000 generations yield FID 2.18 for RePR-78M plus JiT-L versus 2.36 for pixel JiT-L at nearly matched training compute. This compares training FLOPs, not inference cost.

likes.title: Neural Networks Are Already Clean
likes.summary: Mechanistic interpretability of neural networks is examined through neuron- and circuit-level studies of image models and language models, including experiments that track neurons during training and test explanations through activation examples, interventions, and attribution graphs. The analysis argues that many apparent mixtures attributed to superposition instead reflect tool or architectural

likes.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
likes.summary: Priming Models train a one-step image generator by first reconstructing clean images from corrupted inputs, then matching generated and real examples in frozen feature space. On ImageNet, Priming-L reaches FID 1.19 in one network pass using 238.95 EFLOPs, versus Drifting-L’s FID 1.61 using 1,476.39 EFLOPs. This is about 6.2 times less reported training compute for this comparison only.

likes.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
likes.summary: HybridAgent lets a tool-using language-model agent reason in continuous hidden states and use text for tool calls and answers. HybridLink aligns hidden states with the model’s input-embedding space, while retained attention-cache entries carry context across turns. At 14B parameters, it scores 49.5 average on WebWalker versus ARPO’s 40.5, within evaluations of Qwen3-Base models on 11 benchmarks.

likes.title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
likes.summary: VideoJev scores candidate time intervals to locate events and candidate answers for video questions, reusing one video prefix across queries through cached or joint inference. It reports 65.3 mean temporal intersection-over-union, versus 58.6 for its 4B backbone, and a four-benchmark QA mean of 74.3, near 74.9 for Qwen3.5-4B Thinking; evaluations cover grounding and multiple-choice QA, not agent workflows.

likes.title: VLA-$Δ$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
likes.summary: VLA-Δ trains a vision-language-action model to represent changes in task progress, object motion, spatial relations, and contact, then uses that representation to generate actions. Its transition targets supervise training but are not decoded at deployment. It reports 98.40% on LIBERO and a 5.5-percentage-point advantage over π₀.₅ across five real-robot tasks, without leading every task.

likes.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
likes.summary: The authors survey agentic robots as systems that use goals, observations, capabilities, and execution feedback to choose actions, gather information, revise plans, or recover. They organize prior work into four domains and seventeen overlapping categories. An external RoboDojo evaluation reports 22.48% average success across 42 simulation tasks, versus 19.34% for trained DM0.5; this comparison does not isolate feedback’s effect.

likes.title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
likes.summary: GracefulRL trains models to favor success over safe fallback and fallback over error, while preserving a learning signal for success. It optimizes a combination of the log probability of success and the log probability of avoiding error, without labels or an inference-time verifier. On AIME, Qwen3-4B-Base reduced errors by 88.8% with a 3.1-point success decrease, in tested settings.

likes.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
likes.summary: T2-Z adapts an action-conditioned world model to hidden environmental variation by optimizing a compact latent from observed interaction trajectories, without labels for hidden factors. The trained model stays frozen during test-time adaptation. Across four real-world tasks, average tracked-state prediction error fell from 19.30 to 10.85 pixels and action success rose from 26.47% to 70.80%; these are task averages, not guarantees.

likes.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
likes.summary: The authors test whether resetting search history helps agents improve stalled optimization tasks. They periodically clear agent sessions and candidate-history state while retaining the best candidate, allowing four-agent teams to restart exploration. On AHC014, forgetting gains 9.2% on average over 30 more proposals per agent, versus 1.4% for continuing; experiments do not isolate which cleared state drives the gain.

likes.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
likes.summary: Terminal-RSI trains terminal agents through alternating cycles of verified self-rewriting and policy refinement. It preserves successful demonstrations to update the actor, then uses execution feedback to refine the policy while carrying a learned value critic across phases. Across four Terminal-Bench suites, the equal-weight Mean@3 rises from 20.68% to 50.58%; on LHTB, strict completions rise from 0/46 to 5/46.

likes.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
likes.summary: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents completed Minecraft’s survival-mode path to the Ender Dragon in one randomly generated world on Easy difficulty. They wrote programs through Mineflayer, using structured game information and coordinating through chat and shared notes. The run took 27 hours and 14 minutes, with 2,783 programs and 605 deaths; it shows one completion, not reliability across runs.

likes.title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
likes.summary: Jeva makes typed decisions over requests and reusable candidate sets, including choices, Boolean judgments, and numeric scores. It encodes options separately, then lets each request representation read the full set before scoring, while caching option computations. On MLDR, hybrid caching reduced median latency from 2,102.0 ms to 75.1 ms for novel sets, with no decision changes in tested cache conditions.

likes.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
likes.summary: AutoSFT helps an agent improve supervised fine-tuning by changing training data through a structured research loop. A meta-agent selects recipes, while separate execution and analysis agents handle training and propose data changes; synthesis adds verified examples. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, analysis reaches 67.10 on IFEval versus 60.60 within 30 rounds, in single searches per configuration.

likes.title: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
likes.summary: The Agentic Scientist coordinates research agents through parallel sandboxed investigations, shared conclusions, rubric checks, retrospective comparisons, and evidence-grounded writing. In a two-worker RL fine-tuning ablation, shared knowledge improved search progress but did not significantly change final best scores. On a synthetic multi-needle retrieval task, query-conditioned Doc-to-LoRA reached 98.0% exact-match accuracy; this result does not establish general retrieval performance.

likes.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The authors benchmark ten self-distillation methods against GRPO across four tasks and Qwen3.5 models at 2B, 4B, and 9B, using a shared evaluation protocol. Across twelve task-model settings, PCSD has the highest equal-weight mean, 54.26 versus GRPO’s 49.68, but leads no individual setting, winning six, trailing five, and tying one; results are limited to this benchmark.

likes.title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-Evolving Coding Agent For Physical Intelligence
likes.summary: EmbodiedEvo lets a robot coding agent preserve experience from one scene as executable Skills and diagnostic Lessons, then transfer them to a fresh agent in another scene. In matched RoboDojo-Sim development tests, Astra/xhigh success rose from 8.50% to 30.17%. Yet full evaluation Precision success was 13.25%, showing that inherited procedures do not ensure successful contact control.

likes.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
likes.summary: Librarian Agents prepares a reusable hierarchical workspace of synthetic files linked to source documents, then uses a separate agent to answer later questions. The builder is trained with reinforcement learning using downstream answer quality. On BrowseComp-Plus, it improves accuracy over baselines by an average of 33 percentage points across two fixed answering models; this result measures answer accuracy, not cost.

likes.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
likes.summary: ATAS addresses screenplay-to-video continuity by storing static scene geometry and time-indexed event evidence for later shots. Validation separates film inclusion from memory updates. ATAS reports 15.968 PSNR_C on spatial revisit, versus ViewCrafter’s 15.255, and leads three event-recapture axes but trails ReCA on action-and-state preservation; event tests use no synchronized target video.

likes.title: Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations by Correcting Modality Misrouting in Omnimodal LLMs
likes.summary: CaRe addresses audio-visual errors where a correct modality-specific answer is lost in the joint prediction. A text-only probe nominates audio or video; if the unimodal and joint answers disagree, CaRe steers the joint representation toward the unimodal reference while retaining both modalities. On CMM, MiniCPM-o-2.6 reaches 86.9% accuracy versus MAD’s 77.3%; evidence is limited to discrete-answer cross-modal hallucination benchmarks.
